title: The Garden Belonging to People Not Yet Born
title_ja: まだ生まれていない人々の庭
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、法令、運用基準、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine a fictional settlement established inside an artificial habitat far from Earth, whose inhabitants plan to maintain a collection of living plants for purposes extending well beyond the lifetime of the people responsible for its initial construction.
sentences.ja: 地球から遠い人工居住施設内に作られた架空の居住地を想像しよう。住民は建設担当者の寿命をはるかに超える目的のため植物を維持しようとする。

sentences.en: The designers discuss whether the collection should primarily provide familiar experiences for the first generation of inhabitants or preserve a wider range of possibilities for future residents whose preferences and practical needs cannot yet be known.
sentences.ja: 設計者は植物群が第一世代に身近な経験を主に提供すべきか、好みや実際の必要がまだ分からない将来住民に幅広い可能性を保存すべきか議論する。

sentences.en: Some suggest creating a garden that reproduces landscapes remembered from their childhood, arguing that access to recognizable natural surroundings may help people maintain a sense of continuity with the world they have left behind.
sentences.ja: 幼少期の風景を再現する庭を提案し、認識できる自然環境へのアクセスで去った世界との連続性を保てるかもしれないと主張する者もいる。

sentences.en: Others question whether reproducing one familiar landscape would be an appropriate use of limited resources when maintaining that particular arrangement might prevent subsequent generations from adapting the collection to circumstances that the original planners could not anticipate.
sentences.ja: 一方、特定の配置維持が後世による予期できなかった状況への適応を妨げる可能性があるとき、身近な風景一つの再現が限られた資源の適切な使用か疑問を持つ者もいる。

sentences.en: The disagreement illustrates a difficulty that arises whenever a project is intended to outlast the people who originally established its objectives: those responsible for present decisions cannot consult all the people who may eventually be affected by them.
sentences.ja: 対立は当初目的を定めた人々より長く続く計画で生じる困難を示す。現在の決定者は最終的影響を受け得る全員に相談できない。

sentences.en: One engineer proposes distinguishing the physical arrangements needed to sustain the collection from the particular appearance that its original designers would like to preserve as a reminder of their own experiences.
sentences.ja: ある技術者は植物群維持に必要な物理的仕組みと元の設計者が自身の経験の記念として残したい特定の外観を区別することを提案する。

sentences.en: Certain decisions about the habitat would require careful specialist assessment, because changes involving its essential supporting systems could have consequences that would be difficult for later residents to reverse.
sentences.ja: 居住施設についての判断の一部には慎重な専門評価が必要だ。不可欠な支援システムの変更には後世の住民が元に戻しにくい影響があり得るからだ。

sentences.en: Other decisions, such as the selection of decorative features or the names assigned to particular sections of the garden, might be more readily revised without threatening the underlying purpose of maintaining the living collection.
sentences.ja: 装飾要素の選定や庭の特定区画の命名といった他の決定は生きた植物群の維持という根本目的を脅かさずより容易に修正できるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The planners therefore begin to classify decisions according to the consequences of changing them, rather than assuming that every element of the original design should possess the same degree of permanence.
sentences.ja: そこで元の設計の全要素が同じ永続性を持つべきと想定せず、変更の影響に従って決定を分類し始める。

sentences.en: They also recognize that a choice which appears reversible in a drawing might become difficult to alter if the organization lacks the expertise, equipment, or records required to carry out the proposed change.
sentences.ja: 図では可逆的に見える選択も変更実施に必要な専門知識、設備、記録が組織になければ変えにくくなり得ると認識する。

sentences.en: A second discussion concerns the knowledge that must be transferred to people who will inherit responsibility for the garden without having participated in the debates through which its original design was developed.
sentences.ja: 別の議論は元の設計を生んだ議論に参加せず庭の責任を引き継ぐ人々へ伝えるべき知識に関する。

sentences.en: The designers could prepare detailed instructions describing how the collection is currently maintained, but such instructions would not necessarily help their successors determine whether an unfamiliar situation calls for a departure from the established routine.
sentences.ja: 現在の維持方法の詳細な指示は準備できるが、未知の状況で既定手順から離れる必要があるか後継者が判断する助けになるとは限らない。

sentences.en: A record explaining the reasoning behind important design choices might therefore prove especially valuable when later generations possess information that was unavailable to the project's original participants.
sentences.ja: 重要な設計判断の理由を説明する記録は、後世が元の参加者に利用できなかった情報を持つ場合に特に有用と分かるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The planners consider documenting alternatives that were rejected, including the circumstances that led them to conclude that those alternatives would be inappropriate at the time rather than claiming that they could never become useful.
sentences.ja: 却下した代替案も記録し、それらが決して有用にならないと主張せず当時不適切と結論づけた事情を含めることを検討する。

sentences.en: Such documentation would allow future residents to distinguish a deliberate commitment to an enduring objective from an ordinary practical decision that reflected the limitations of an earlier period.
sentences.ja: その記録は永続的目標への意図的約束と以前の時代の限界を反映した通常の実務判断を将来住民が区別できるようにする。

sentences.en: The fictional settlement also confronts the question of how current inhabitants should evaluate their success when some of the benefits they hope to create cannot be observed until long after their own involvement has ended.
sentences.ja: 架空居住地は創出を望む利益の一部が自身の関与終了後かなりたたないと観察できないとき現在の住民が成功をどう評価すべきかという問いにも直面する。

sentences.en: Maintaining the existing collection in good condition may demonstrate that the current procedures are functioning under present circumstances, yet it cannot establish that the same procedures will remain appropriate indefinitely.
sentences.ja: 現植物群の良好な維持は現在の事情で手順が機能することを示しても手順が無期限に適切と確定できない。

sentences.en: Conversely, leaving large parts of the habitat available for unspecified future developments would not necessarily constitute responsible preparation if those spaces consumed resources that the present residents urgently needed.
sentences.ja: 逆に未指定の将来開発のため広い空間を残しても現在住民が緊急に必要とする資源を消費するなら必ずしも責任ある準備とはならない。

sentences.en: The planners consequently propose assessing the collection in relation to several distinct objectives, including its present usefulness, the preservation of relevant knowledge, and the practical capacity of future residents to reconsider its organization.
sentences.ja: そこで現在の有用性、関連知識の保存、将来住民が仕組みを再考できる実務能力など複数の別個の目的に照らし評価する案を出す。

sentences.en: The example describes no actual space habitat or verified operational method; it is a thought experiment about the responsibilities involved in planning projects across generations under substantial uncertainty.
sentences.ja: この例は実際の宇宙居住施設や検証済み運用法を述べず大きな不確実性の下で世代を超える計画の責任についての思考実験だ。

sentences.en: A project designed to endure for an unusually long period requires more than a set of instructions intended to prevent future people from changing everything its founders considered important.
sentences.ja: 非常に長く続くよう設計された計画には創設者が重要と考えた全てを将来の人々が変えるのを防ぐ指示集以上のものが必要だ。

sentences.en: It may also require institutions capable of explaining why particular commitments were made and distinguishing those commitments from decisions that deserve reconsideration when circumstances change.
sentences.ja: 特定の約束がなぜなされ、事情変化時に再考に値する決定とどう区別するか説明できる制度も必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: Preserving the capacity for responsible revision does not eliminate the need for people to make difficult choices in the present, nor does it guarantee that future generations will agree with those choices.
sentences.ja: 責任ある修正能力の保存は現在の困難な選択の必要をなくさず将来世代が同意する保証もしない。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it acknowledges that an inherited project may derive part of its value from the opportunities it provides for people to respond to conditions that its creators were unable to imagine.
sentences.ja: それでも受け継いだ計画の価値の一部は創設者が想像できなかった条件への対応機会から生じ得ることを認める。

sentences.en: For the fictional settlement, the garden becomes a symbol of continuity not because its appearance is preserved forever, but because its inhabitants can participate in determining what deserves to survive.
sentences.ja: 架空居住地にとって庭は外観が永遠に残るからでなく住民が何を残すべきかの判断に参加できるから連続性の象徴になる。

chiefly or for the most part
change away from an established pattern

questions.prompt: What causes disagreement among the original designers?
options: Whether to prioritize a familiar landscape or preserve flexibility for future residents.
Whether to return to Earth immediately.
Whether plants should have names at all.
Whether the settlement has any residents.
questions.explanation_ja: 現在の再現と将来の柔軟性。

questions.prompt: Why is the project difficult to plan across generations?
options: Current inhabitants possess no preferences.
Future residents are guaranteed to reject every choice.
People affected by future consequences cannot all be consulted now.
All objectives have already been verified.
questions.explanation_ja: 将来世代に相談できない。

questions.prompt: How do planners propose classifying decisions?
options: By the age of every designer.
By the consequences and practical feasibility of revising them.
By the attractiveness of the original drawing alone.
By an assumption that all details must remain permanent.

questions.prompt: Why might a seemingly reversible decision be difficult to change?
options: A drawing automatically determines future circumstances.
All decisions cost exactly the same resources.
No practical change can ever occur.
Later residents may lack necessary expertise, equipment or records.
questions.explanation_ja: 変更能力に必要な条件。

questions.prompt: Why preserve reasoning in addition to instructions?
options: It makes every future decision unnecessary.
It ensures the original routine can never be questioned.
It helps successors adapt when circumstances differ from those originally anticipated.
It replaces all technical knowledge.
questions.explanation_ja: 理由を残すことで新条件に対応。

questions.prompt: What information about rejected alternatives should be recorded?
options: The circumstances that made them inappropriate at the time.
A permanent rule against ever reconsidering them.
Only the names of their supporters.
Proof that no alternative can ever succeed.

questions.prompt: What is the limitation of good current maintenance?
options: It proves current procedures never work.
It guarantees every future development will be beneficial.
It prevents assessing any present usefulness.
It does not establish that the same procedures will always remain appropriate.
questions.explanation_ja: 現在の機能と将来の適切性を区別。

questions.prompt: Which objectives are proposed for evaluation?
options: Only the visual appearance of the garden.
Present usefulness, preservation of knowledge and future capacity to reorganize.
Only benefits that cannot yet be observed.
The number of rejected alternatives alone.

questions.prompt: What does derive mean in the context of the passage?
options: Prevent from occurring.
Make permanently identical.
Obtain from a source.
Evaluate without evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the author's argument?
options: Long-lived projects should preserve both important purposes and the capacity of future people to revise decisions responsibly.
Every founding decision should remain permanently unchanged.
Future flexibility always outweighs current needs.
A detailed instruction manual guarantees that future conditions will be understood.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的の継続と責任ある修正能力。

grammar.focus: whenever a project is intended to outlast
grammar.explanation_ja: wheneverは一般条件、outlastはより長く続く。

grammar.focus: rather than assuming that every element
whether an unfamiliar situation calls for a departure

paraphrases.source: The disagreement illustrates a difficulty that arises whenever a project is intended to outlast the people who originally established its objectives: those responsible for present decisions cannot consult all the people who may eventually be affected by them.
paraphrases.rewrite: Planning beyond one's lifetime creates decisions affecting people who cannot yet be consulted.

paraphrases.source: The planners therefore begin to classify decisions according to the consequences of changing them, rather than assuming that every element of the original design should possess the same degree of permanence.
paraphrases.rewrite: The planners assess decisions by their reversibility rather than preserving all details equally.

paraphrases.source: The designers could prepare detailed instructions describing how the collection is currently maintained, but such instructions would not necessarily help their successors determine whether an unfamiliar situation calls for a departure from the established routine.
paraphrases.rewrite: Instructions may not tell successors when unusual conditions justify a different procedure.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 手順だけでは新状況判断を支えない。

paraphrases.source: Preserving the capacity for responsible revision does not eliminate the need for people to make difficult choices in the present, nor does it guarantee that future generations will agree with those choices.
paraphrases.rewrite: Keeping revision possible neither removes difficult present choices nor guarantees future agreement.
